report.tagline: India's once-leading electric scooter maker, from the founder of the Ola cab app, now rebuilding after a sharp fall over service problems.
report.simpleSummary: Bhavish Aggarwal first built Ola, India's big cab-booking app. In 2017 he started Ola Electric, which makes electric scooters and motorcycles in a huge factory near Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu, and sold them online and through its own stores. It became India's top-selling electric scooter brand by 2024, but broken scooters, long service waits and thousands of complaints sent buyers to TVS, Bajaj and Ather. In late 2026 it is closing its own stores, moving to dealers, and trying to win back trust.

keyNumbers.note: Company figures. Own stores stopped taking orders on 1 November 2026.

overview.whatItDoes: Ola Electric designs and builds electric two-wheelers like the S1 scooter range and Roadster motorcycles, and now makes its own battery cells at a 6 GWh gigafactory. It listed on Indian stock exchanges in August 2024. The Ola ride-hailing app is a separate company (ANI Technologies) under the same founder; this teardown focuses on Ola Electric.
howItWorks: Customers book a scooter online or at a store; prices range roughly from ₹80,000 to ₹1.6 lakh depending on model and battery.
Scooters are built at the Futurefactory in Tamil Nadu and sent to stores or dealers.
Until 2026 Ola sold mostly through its own experience centres; from November 2026 it sells through independent dealers who buy and hold stock.
Service is done at Ola service centres and through home visits; software updates arrive over the air.
Ola now makes its own lithium-ion cells (4680 Bharat cell) to cut battery cost, the largest part of an EV's price.
Government PLI incentives pay Ola for locally made vehicles and cells.
overview.valueProposition: A feature-rich electric scooter at a lower price than rivals, with lower running cost than petrol.

Aggressive prices, including models under ₹1 lakh, helped by subsidies and PLI.
Battery options up to about 4 kWh and Ola's Hypercharger network.
Online booking and home delivery (until the 2026 dealer shift).

painPoints.pain: Scooters that do not get better over time
painPoints.howSolved: MoveOS software updates add features over the air.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: S1 Pro, S1 Air and S1 X with different batteries and prices.
Touchscreen dashboard, navigation, ride modes and over-the-air updates.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Made Ola feel like a tech product, its main point of difference.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Could cut battery cost 10 to 15% if quality yields reach about 85%.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Electric motorcycles for the bigger motorcycle market.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Opens a larger segment than scooters.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Book service, track repairs and get home service.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The weakest link; service failures drove the brand's fall.

steps.detail: Compares Ola S1 with TVS iQube and Ather Rizta on YouTube and Reddit.
Visits a dealer (from late 2026) for a test ride.
Picks S1 X with 3 kWh battery for price.
Takes a loan with low down payment.
Dealer handles RTO number plate and delivery.
Charges overnight from a home socket.
Scooter shows a motor error and will not move.
Raises a ticket in the Ola app.
Waits days for pickup; parts may take weeks.
Calls support or complains on social media.
Gets scooter back; decides whether to trust the brand again.

businessModel.summary: Ola Electric makes money by selling scooters and motorcycles at a margin, plus parts, service, extended warranty and accessories. Government PLI incentives add to margin. The shift to dealers moves stock costs off Ola's books but gives dealers a cut.

revenueStreams.detail: Scooters and motorcycles; the main revenue.
PLI payments for local manufacturing of vehicles and cells.
Paid MoveOS upgrades on some models.

businessModel.pricing: S1 range from about ₹80,000 to ₹1.6 lakh ex-showroom depending on battery and model, with frequent discounts. Roadster motorcycles priced in a similar range. Prices change often.
costDrivers: R&D for cells and new models
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a scooter sold at ₹1 lakh, Ola's gross margin of about 30% (26.5% without PLI) leaves about ₹26,500 to ₹30,000 before fixed costs. But with only about 13,000 to 20,000 units a month, fixed costs for factories, R&D and staff are too large to cover, so it lost ₹362 crore in the quarter. Ola needs about 25,000+ units a month and cheaper in-house cells to break even (estimate).

howTheyGetUsers: Founder-led hype on social media and launch events
Dealer network expansion from 2026 into smaller towns
whatBringsUsersBack: Referrals from happy owners (when service works)
growth.moat: Ola's possible moat is cost: owning cell manufacturing and a big factory could make its batteries cheaper than rivals. But that only matters if quality and service earn back trust, which is currently its biggest weakness.

competitors.name: TVS iQube
competitors.positioning: Trusted legacy brand with a wide dealer and service network; became the EV leader.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Ola has more tech features and lower prices but much weaker service trust.

competitors.name: Bajaj Chetak
competitors.positioning: Metal-body electric scooter from a trusted brand with many dealers.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Ola offers more range per rupee; Bajaj has better reliability reputation.

competitors.name: Ather Energy
competitors.positioning: Premium EV maker with strong software and service, also listed in 2025.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Both are tech-first; Ather is seen as more reliable and has a family scooter (Rizta).

competitors.name: Hero Vida and petrol scooters like Honda Activa
competitors.positioning: Big brands with huge service networks.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Ola is cheaper to run but riskier on service.

northStar.metric: Number of Ola scooters on the road working without an open service issue
northStar.why: Ola's problem is trust after purchase. Happy, working scooters drive word of mouth and new sales; sales alone hid the service crisis.

Safety incidents such as battery fires
strengths: Own battery cell factory, rare in India
Debt cut from ₹3,132 crore to ₹1,819 crore
weaknesses: Damaged trust from service delays and quality issues
Revenue down sharply and still loss-making
Relying on dispatches can hide weak real sales
Founder's public fights with critics hurt the brand
risks: TVS, Bajaj and Ather taking more share with better service
Regulatory action from CCPA and state transport offices
Dealer transition may fail if dealers lose money
userComplaints: Long wait times at service centres, sometimes weeks

improvementIdeas.idea: Service promise: fix within 72 hours or free loaner scooter
improvementIdeas.problem: Long service waits are the top complaint.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Average days to resolve service tickets

improvementIdeas.problem: People do not believe service has improved.

improvementIdeas.idea: Predictive fault alerts from scooter data
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer roadside failures and planned repairs.

improvementIdeas.idea: Train dealers as certified service points
improvementIdeas.problem: Too few service centres outside metros.

pmLessons: The product does not end at sale. For vehicles, service is part of the product, and failing at it can undo great sales.
Growing faster than your support can handle is risky. Ola sold scooters faster than it could fix them.
Owning distribution saves dealer margin but adds heavy costs; Ola reversed course to dealers in 2026.
Founder voice can build hype but also hurt the brand when the founder fights critics in public.

interviewQuestions.question: Ola's sales fell sharply due to service complaints. As PM, what would you fix first?
interviewQuestions.hint: Prioritise by impact on owners: parts, repair time, support communication. Pick metrics like days to resolve and NPS.

interviewQuestions.question: Was moving from own stores to dealers the right call?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare cost, reach, control of experience, working capital. Discuss risks and what to measure.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you win back an unhappy Ola owner?
interviewQuestions.hint: Listen, fix the issue fast, offer goodwill. Track repeat complaints and referral rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature in the Ola app to reduce service calls.
interviewQuestions.hint: Self-diagnosis, live repair tracking, parts ETA, video help. Measure call volume per scooter.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Ola Electric's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Working scooters on the road or satisfied owners. Break into sales, service, reliability and satisfaction.
